messages:
Sam: Heads-up — Aurora just sent draft numbers for reserved commitments + spot credits. Need to consolidate into our cost model by EOD Thurs. Key asks: SKU mappings to our marketplace SKUs, minimum commit sizes, price floors for reserved vs ephemeral, any listing or revenue-share fees, and lead times for capacity increases. Can people take pieces?

Jules: I have Aurora's excel. Uploaded to //docs/partnerships/aurora_pricing_draft.xlsx and shared with you all. Notes in sheet 'assumptions'. they list 'GPU-node' and 'GPU-hour' SKUs, not 1:1 with our marketplace ids.

Corey: Putting together amortization and per-token cost transforms. Quick Q: does Aurora quote per-GPU-hour or per-instance-month? The mapping changes reserved math a lot.

Jules: Aurora quoted both: per-GPU-hour for spot/ephemeral, per-instance-month for reserved (they call it 'commit hours' in the sheet). I'll annotate conversion formulas in the sheet.

Dina: For finance, propose we amortize reserved commit over 24 months and apply straight-line utilization ramp (20/50/80/95). Also need their SLA credits if availability < X%. Do they provide credits?

Jules: They note a 99.5% baseline with credits tiers, will paste the SLA terms.

Corey: Important: for per-inference billing our optimizer expects cost per token and cost per batch. If we translate wrongly we'll under/overprice by ~15%. I'll add conversion rows: sample workload (chat seq len 64) -> tokens/GPU-hour.

Mike: Product question: any constraints on model families for reserved? e.g., Aurora only allows NVL models on reserved pools? If yes, that affects routing fallback.

Jules: Aurora flagged that certain high-memory SKUs are reserved-only due to availability. I'll mark tags in sheet: reserved_only = TRUE for those SKUs.

Anna: Legal — before we publish any marketplace listing we need signed AUP + SOC2 attestation from Aurora and to confirm data egress responsibilities. Also check whether revenue share is gross or net of marketplace credits.

Dina: Good flag. Also need to confirm billing metric: are they invoicing us monthly based on committed hours or at usage with monthly true-up? That changes cashflow modeling.

Jules: Their quoted billing model: monthly true-up against committed hours; any overage billed at spot rates, underuse credited at 50% of spot (per initial draft). I'll highlight in the sheet.

Corey: Suggest we run two scenarios: (A) aggressive utilization (95% avg) with 36mo amortization for hardware and (B) conservative (60% avg) with 24mo. I'll sketch both and post numbers.

Sam: Thanks — timeline: 1) finalize SKU mapping + commit sizes by Wed EOD, 2) finance inputs (Dina) + pricing scenarios (Corey) by Thurs EOD, 3) legal checklist (Anna) by Fri. If anyone can't hit these, ping now.

Jules: Pinged Aurora contact (marco@aurora.ai) for SOC2 + AUP PDFs. Also asked for exact marketplace fee schedule (listing + promo credits).

MarketplaceBot: New vendor draft uploaded: aurora-ai (vendor id: v-aurora). Listing draft in review queue.

Mike: Thumbs up. If Aurora enforces reserved-only for certain models we should add fallback routing policy to avoid 503s — will sync with runtime.

Sam: Great. I'll consolidate the final spreadsheet into the cost model and share a short summary for the execs. :thumbsup:

Jules: Added short comments in the sheet under 'open_items' with owners.

Dina: I'll start with a baseline cashflow table and then slot Corey's cost-per-token rows.

Anna: I'll draft a redline checklist for the marketplace agreement and post in legal channel.

Sam: Perfect. Thanks team.
